section_summary.extract_value: This section details a multilevel model analysis exploring the relationships between daily gratitude and outcomes like loneliness and self-reported health. The study found significant within-person associations, indicating that higher daily gratitude correlated with less loneliness and better health. A moderating effect of condition (treatment vs. control) was also observed for between-person gratitude associations on health symptoms and loneliness, with stronger effects in the treatment group. The analysis involved N=36 participants over 20 days, yielding 608 survey day observations.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details a study that investigated multilevel associations between daily gratitude and outcomes such as loneliness, subjective well-being, self-reported health, and health symptoms. The study utilized multilevel models and found significant within-person associations and moderating effects of condition on between-person gratitude associations. The sample size for this study was N=36 participants, who provided 608 survey day observations over 20 days.
